_description: How ForgePilot should decide when to use native Material Expressions versus Material Functions in current Unreal Engine material graphs.

core_model.material_expression: A primitive graph node such as Add, Multiply, DepthFade, ParticleSubUV, ComponentMask, or DynamicParameter. Use expressions for small, direct operations where the artist needs visible control.
core_model.material_function: A reusable packaged graph made from expressions. Use MaterialFunctionCall when the logic is reusable, has many internal nodes, or is easier to read as one named block.
core_model.important_caveat: A Material Function is not automatically cheaper at compiled shader level. It usually improves readability, reuse, and consistency; shader cost still depends on the expressions inside the function.

tooling_contract.create_call_node: Use add_material_expression with expression_type='MaterialFunctionCall' and function_path set to the full function asset path.
tooling_contract.inspect_function: Use get_material_function_info before wiring any non-trivial MaterialFunctionCall.
tooling_contract.wire_safely: Prefer connect_material_nodes.target_input_name for MaterialFunctionCall inputs instead of raw target_input_index.
tooling_contract.validate_support: Use Tools/Validation/run_material_function_probe.ps1 to verify curated functions can be loaded, inspected, and instantiated through the bridge.

when_to_prefer_functions.why: A function keeps frame math, UV offsets, and optional motion-vector blending out of the main material graph.

when_to_prefer_functions.case: Range remap, contrast, and image adjustment
when_to_prefer_functions.why: These blocks are common in dissolve, smoke alpha shaping, packed mask cleanup, and emissive shaping.
Coordinate conversion is easy to misbuild from scratch and should stay readable for portal rings, shockwaves, decals, sky UVs, and radial masks.
World aligned texture and normal logic becomes noisy if rebuilt inline and often has several artist-facing inputs.
Blend functions communicate intent better than hand-built math chains and reduce repetitive graph clutter.
BreakOut and MakeFloat functions make packed texture workflows easier to inspect and safer to wire by name.

when_to_prefer_functions.case: Depth, camera fade, and environment integration
when_to_prefer_functions.why: Depth-related material blocks are visually sensitive. A named function block helps preserve the intended fade behavior.

when_to_keep_expressions_inline: Use Add, Multiply, OneMinus, Saturate, Clamp, Power, ComponentMask, AppendVector, and simple parameters directly when the logic is only one or two nodes.
Use ParticleColor, DynamicParameter, ParticleRelativeTime, ParticleSubUV, DepthFade, PixelDepth, and WorldPosition directly when they are the primary data source.
Do not hide key artist controls inside functions unless the function exposes clear input pins and documented defaults.
Do not replace every math chain with a function. Readability is the goal, not abstraction for its own sake.
agent_workflow: Classify the material task and load the curated VFX recipe first.
If the graph needs a reusable block, search material_node_catalog_current.json for candidate MaterialFunctions.
Run get_material_function_info on the candidate and inspect input/output names.
Instantiate with add_material_expression using MaterialFunctionCall and the exact function_path.
If the function is not already in run_material_function_probe.ps1, add it to that script before depending on it in production automation.
After wiring, inspect or compile the material and save the asset.

vfx_defaults.fire_smoke_flipbook: Prefer ParticleSubUV for Niagara sprite renderer flipbook sampling. Use FlipBook_UniformNonUniform or FlipBook_MotionVectors when the material needs custom UV frame logic outside ParticleSubUV.
vfx_defaults.opacity_fade: For additive fire, Niagara alpha often appears as emissive intensity instead of true transparency. Use Translucent alpha/depth fade when actual fade-out must be visible.
vfx_defaults.function_wiring: Always prefer pin-name wiring for functions with artist-facing inputs such as HueShift, RemapValueRange, CameraDepthFade, WorldAlignedTexture, and Blend functions.

validation.function_docs_asset_registry_rule: When building semantic Material Function docs, use scan_assets with asset_type='MaterialFunction' instead of trusting every .uasset under Engine/Content/Functions.
validation.known_redirector_caution: The catalog may include legacy or redirector-like function names. For world aligned alpha blending, use WorldAlignedBlend instead of World_Aligned_Blend because the latter may not load through EditorAssetLibrary in bridge automation.
